newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week March 27 - April 4th 1997.
**MARCH 27**
BRUSSELS - DHL says it will make more use of European sub-hubs due to rapid expansion of its Brussels headquarters.
* DHL says it is considering the future of its Boeing 727 fleet in Europe.
PANAMA CITY - Panamanian authorities says Panama and Peru have reached an open skies aviation agreement, the first between two Latin American countries.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Cargo says it record a 1.8 percent drop in its freight load factor to 68.3 percent in February.
DALLAS - Officials says a wing flap from a Delta Air Line jet fell off and crashed to the ground by a major road near Dallas, but no-one was injured.

NEW YORK - BA chief executive Robert Ayling says he remains confident the proposed transatlantic alliance with American Airlines will be approved this summer, but British Air could reject the alliance if regulators required the airlines to pay a burdensome price, such as disposing of a large number of airport slots.
* Alitalia Airlines says it is waiting to see if jet fuel prices drop to the levels of June last year before removing the cargo fuel surcharge.
HONG KONG - SAS says it remains committed to its Asian freighter service to Osaka in Japan via Macau after a first year of unprofitable operation.

CHICAGO - Richard Fleming, president and CEO of the St.Louis Regional Commerce and Growth Association says civic and business groups in St.Louis affirmed their confident in TWA, after the company said auditors plans to qualify the carriers 1996 year end results.
**MARCH 28**
BEIJING - Industry officials says China's aviation industry may see more mergers this year but the pace of consolidation will be slow.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot says it has abandoned plans to modernise its wide-body IIyushin 11-86 jets with CFM-56 engines from GE and Snecma.
PARIS - The French government says it had given the go-ahead for the 1.5 billion franc extension of the Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport north of Paris.
ZAGREB - Croatia Airlines says it would increase international services during the coming tourist season, adding flights from coastal resorts to its main destinations in Europe.
BELGRADE - Yugoslav airlines Jugoslovenski Aerotransport says it will introduce a flights to St. Petersburg in its summer timetable.
PARIS - Anne-Marie Idrac, a junior transport minister says the French government should keep a stake in flag carrier Air France after its privatisation.
**MARCH 29**
ATLANTA - The FAA says that new procedures were being developed to detect flaws in key engine parts such as the cracked fan hub that caused a Delta Air Lines jet engines to fly apart last year.
**MARCH 30**
HONG KONG - Hong Kong Dragon Airlines says it is unlikely to be listed in 1998 unless it is part of a possible listing of its major shareholder, China National Aviation Corp.
KUALA LUMPUR - MAS says it plans to employ an additional 2,000 workers this year, increasing its workforce by ten percent.
* MAS says it plans to raise 3,271 million ringgit in a capital restructuring exercise to help pay for plane purchases and investments at a new airport.
PARIS - State-owned Air France Europe resumed flights out of Paris-Orly airport as ground staff discussed whether to continue a strike.
BOMBAY - An Indian Airlines cargo official says demand for air cargo services is expected to increase significantly if truck unions go ahead with their national strike.
**MARCH 31**
SINGAPORE - Singapore airlines says its regional carrier Silkair plans to purchase about 12 aircraft to expand its fleet.
VIENNA - Austrian Airlines says it had resumed commercial flights to Sarajevo after a four-year break, becoming the first Western European airline to offer a direct service to the Bosnian capital.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot says it has achieved international standards of air security.
**APRIL 1**
PARIS - Union leaders says French truck drivers unions called a fresh strike for May 5 after failing to agree with management over retirement at age 55.
MOSCOW - Russian private airline Transaero says it would postpone a code-sharing programme with American Airlines.
* Transaero says it will start passenger flights to Taiwan, Hong Kong and Manchester in June.

DHAKA - Bangladesh national airline Biman says it raised freight rates on cargo bound for New York by about 35 percent, but it immediately came under fire from the country's garments exporters' association.
AMSTERDAM - A company statement says work has started on Schiphol Express Property's new building, due to open in early 1998.
PARIS - State-owned Air France Europe limped into Europe's new "open skies" as ground staff and pilots extended a strike in protest at the airline's merger with big brother Air France.
NEW YORK - The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey says it has named Richard J Lobron deputy executive director of the bistate agency.
PARIS - A company official says a strike by Air France Europe ground staff at Paris-Orly airport has brought the airline's freight traffic at its Paris hub to a standstill.
ROME - Newly-found Azzurra Air says it inaugurated flights from Turin to London and Zurich on March 30.
DUBAI - Dubai-owned Emirates airline says it signed a $118 million france agreement with a consortium of local and international banks for the fourth of seven Boeing 777 twinjets on order.
FRANKFURT - SAA says it will hold air cargo rates from Europe to South Africa stable this spring.
* Lufthansa says it expects profits to rebound in 1997 after a drop of around ten percent in 1996.
* SAA says it is seeking cargo general sales agents in central and eastern Europe.
* SAA says it planned to add an eighth weekly Frankfurt to Johannesburg passenger flight this autumn.
* SAA Cargo says it will take a first step towards independent operations from today.
BELGRADE - The Belgrade daily Vecernje Novosti says the Yugoslav government plans to sell four of its six Lear-jet 25s.
MOSCOW - The FAA says Russian has announced new aviation regulations which will improve passenger safety and assure Russian majority stakes in joint ventures with foreign partners.
* Lufthansa will add flights on its regular routes to Russia ex-soviet destinations in its summer schedule.
MANILA - The Philippine Supreme Court upheld the right of Grand International airways to operate an airline over opposition from flag carrier Philippine Airlines.
BRUSSELS - European airlines are wary of testing new freedoms to fly throughout the bloc since problems such as subsidies, airport congestion and a shortage of slots darken their horizon for now.
NEW YORK - Lufthansa Cargo says it will operate 34 weekly Boeing 747 freighter flights from the U.S. during its summer schedule, which runs from March 30 to October 25.
ROME - Air Seychelles says it will continue to connect with two weekly direct flights between Rome and Mace during the summer period.
FRANKFURT - Swissair says it had increased passenger sales in Germany substantially after increasing flights by 30 percent last year.
TORONTO - The Greater Toronto Airports Authority says that it has agreed to buy the Trillium Terminal Three at Toronto's Lesser B Person International airport.
LONDON - Korean Air Lines says it will inaugurate a weekly Seoul-Sydney McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter service from April 2.
FRANKFURT - German airline Eurowings Luftverkehrs says it had increase cooperation flights from Germany with partners Air
